newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia to repair bomb-hit Red Army monument.
newsitem.headline: Latvia to repair bomb-hit Red Army monument.

text.p: Latvian authorities said on Monday they would repair blast damage caused to a controversial monument to Soviet Red Army troops who drove Nazi soldiers from Riga during World War Two.

The Victory Monument, a towering column of white topped by gold stars and flanked by huge statues of Red Army fighters, was damaged by a bomb last Friday. Much of its base was shattered and huge chunks of masonry were blown off.
Police say they do not know who planted the bomb and a have launched an investigtion.
The monument is loathed by many Latvians as a symbol of the 50 years they were enforced members of the former Soviet Union before the country regained its independence in 1991.
"A commission of experts is being set up to assess the extent of damage. The assesment will take us some two weeks," Riga mayor Andris Berzinsh told a news conference.
"The speed of the renovation will depend on the amount of money available," he added, saying the capital may have to appeal to the state government for funds.
The monument is popular with many local Russian-speakers, who feel the Red Army troops should be honoured. It is often used as a base for rallies of diehard Communists.
Berzinsh ruled out demolishing the monument, although many Latvians would like to see it disappear.
Russia was angered by the blast and Russian ambassador Alexander Udaltsov said it was a political act as well as an act of vandalism.
